global_caption: The video consists of 6 shots and presents an outdoor electromagnetic induction experiment within the science experiment and gaming category. It is rendered in a low-saturation watercolor picture book style with subtle cyberpunk equipment glow details. The visuals maintain cool tones with a base of gray-blue-green hues, using natural cold light from the wilderness and faint fluorescent glows from device coils as primary lighting sources. The emotional tone remains balanced between calmness and exploratory curiosity.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a fade-in into the frame, a wide overhead composition. The forest campsite is placed in the lower-left corner, with thin mist and tree trunks forming depth-leading lines. Focus is on the faintly glowing coil at the center of the campsite and the experimenter carrying a portable electromagnetic device. Foreground features dark blurred foliage, midground includes a folding table, power module, and spool of wire, while the background shows rising mountain ridges. Natural dawn/dusk cold light envelops the scene, with slight cyan-purple glow along device edges. The experimenter pauses to check equipment, his cloak and straps fluttering gently in the breeze. Quiet Chinese The camera slowly tilts down and slightly pushes in, clearly isolating the campsite and coil from the environment.
shot2: Shot 2 transitions via hard cut to a close-up eye-level shot, tightly framed between the workbench and hands. Shallow depth of field blurs background trees into soft watercolor blocks. Focus is on the copper wire, terminal connectors, and portable power interface. Under cold light, the copper wire exhibits a dull metallic sheen, with device indicator lights faintly glowing. The experimenter skillfully winds the wire, tightens connections, and flips the switch. A small tremor occurs when gloves touch metal parts. shot3: Shot 3 transitions via a quick hard cut to an extreme close-up overhead macro shot. The glass plate dominates the frame, with blurred clamps in the foreground forming a framing border. Focus is sharply on individual iron filings. The material transformation from disorder to order is evident. Cold white natural light sweeps diagonally from above, casting fine linear reflections from device fluorescence along the glass edge. The camera executes an extremely slow push-in to preserve detailed particle motion and final texture structure.
shot4: Shot 4 transitions via a brief fade to the mid-mountain platform in a full-frame eye-level shot. Platform railings and rock edges guide the viewer’s gaze toward the central experimental area. The forest below is now distant in the background. In the foreground, warning ribbons flutter in the wind. Midground features a support stand, induction coil, and a metal ring. Background includes clouds and higher snowline. Lighting remains consistent with cold natural light and device micro-glow. After adjusting emission frequency, the metal ring lifts gently from the stand, initially swaying unstably before achieving brief suspension in mid-air. Motion layers are clearly defined. The camera shifts from slight lateral movement to a semi-circular orbit, simultaneously conveying suspension height and drop-off from the platform edge.
shot5: Shot 5 enters via hard cut into a medium-close low-angle shot. Strong winds at the snowline directly press against the lens. Occasional snow particles streak across the foreground, creating a sense of speed. Focus is on the high-power coil and suspended metal object. Background features cold gray sky and intermittent snowy slopes. The experimenter crouches to stabilize the equipment, his coat hem and straps continuously pulled by the wind. The metal object becomes more stable in the harsher environment, transitioning from wobbling to steady levitation. Tiny ice crystals around it are disturbed by the magnetic field, forming ring-shaped scattering patterns.
shot6: Shot 6 follows the wind The night summit unfolds into a broad concluding composition. Foreground features rocks and residual snow. The overall image is cold blue near black, with only device micro-glow and cyan-white halo around the sphere providing illumination, forming a reserved yet distinct visual climax. The experimenter puts down his recording device and looks up at the final result. The camera continues pulling back and slightly elevates, incorporating the summit, sphere, and starry sky into a unified composition, completing the full experimental loop from campsite to high-altitude validation.
